s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling and drainage of serosanguinous fluid from the left labia with signs of sepsis and subcutaneous gas
salient_findings: Progressive swelling of the left labia
Rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid
key_facts: Six-day history of progressive swelling of the left labia
Rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid two days before admission
Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg despite intravenous fluid resuscitation
Pelvic CT imaging showed ulceration of the left labia with air in the subcutaneous fat
Inflammatory fat stranding along the left lateral abdominal wall
LRINEC score 3 with potential to rise to 7

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling and drainage of serosanguinous fluid from the left labia with signs of sepsis and subcutaneous gas

LRINEC score 3 with potential to rise to 7

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive swelling, serosanguinous fluid drainage, and subcutaneous gas on CT imaging, along with elevated white blood cell count and LRINEC score

shortlist.label: Fournier gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to necrotizing fasciitis, with a focus on genital and perineal involvement

shortlist.label: Gas gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of subcutaneous gas on CT imaging and signs of sepsis, which are consistent with gas gangrene

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count, hypotension, and signs of sepsis, which are consistent with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome

shortlist.label: Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive swelling and signs of inflammation, which are consistent with fasciitis

raw.rationale: The presence of subcutaneous gas on CT imaging, ulceration of the left labia, and inflammatory fat stranding along the left lateral abdominal wall, combined with a high white blood cell count and a potential LRINEC score of 7, are highly suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis.

rejected.label: Fournier gangrene
rejected.why: While Fournier gangrene is a type of necrotizing fasciitis, it is more specific to the genital area, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not limited to this area.

rejected.label: Gas gangrene
rejected.why: Gas gangrene typically involves muscle tissue and is caused by Clostridium perfringens, whereas the patient's symptoms and imaging findings suggest involvement of the fascia and subcutaneous tissue.

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a high white blood cell count and hypotension, the presence of subcutaneous gas and ulceration of the left labia are more suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis than streptococcal toxic shock syndrome.

rejected.label: Fasciitis
rejected.why: Fasciitis is a broader term that encompasses necrotizing fasciitis, but the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more specific for necrotizing fasciitis.
